speaker: Unknown
en: We took a conscious decision to embrace a lot of risk and say, hey, it sounds crazy, but crazy is good because the night is always the darkest before dawn.
zh: 我们做了一个有意识的决定,去拥抱大量风险,说:嘿,这听起来很疯狂,但疯狂是好事,因为黎明前的黑夜总是最黑暗的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can imagine if you build over 16 years from zero to almost a 4 billion US dollar brand, you have to have a very, very strong execution engine or it will fall apart in that journey.
zh: 你可以想象,如果你用 16 年时间从零打造出一个接近 40 亿美元的品牌,你必须拥有一个非常非常强大的执行引擎,否则它会在那段旅程中分崩离析。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really an opportunity to build a brand that doesn't have to be ultimately the absolute biggest, but is the most premium brand of the future.
zh: 所以这真的是一个机会,去打造一个最终不必是绝对最大、但却是未来最高端(最 premium)的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's David Alleman, co-founder and co-CEO of ON.
zh: 那是 David Alleman,ON 的联合创始人兼联合 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: ON is the bellwether for a new generation of athletic footwear and apparel companies that are posing a significant challenge to the likes of Nike and Adidas.
zh: ON 是新一代运动鞋服公司的风向标,它们正对 Nike 和 Adidas 之类的品牌构成重大挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: David explains how ON is taking advantage of the increased visibility of sports in society, partnering with stars like Zendaya, Roger Federer, and others, and appealing to what he calls the movement class.
zh: David 讲解了 ON 如何利用体育在社会中日益提升的能见度,与 Zendaya、Roger Federer 等明星合作,并吸引他所说的「运动阶层」(movement class)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether you've ever slipped on a pair of OnCloud shoes or not, David's insights will inspire you to keep moving personally and in your business.
zh: 无论你有没有穿过 OnCloud 鞋,David 的洞见都会激励你在个人生活和你自己的业务中保持前行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's get to it.
zh: 那么我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian, and this is Rapid Response.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian,这是 Rapid Response。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm here with David Aliman, the co-founder and co-CEO of ON.
zh: 我今天请到了 ON 的联合创始人兼联合 CEO David Aliman。

speaker: Unknown
en: David, great to sit down with you.
zh: David,很高兴能和你坐下来聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you very much for having me, Bob.
zh: 非常感谢你邀请我, Bob。

speaker: Unknown
en: ON has been an amazing growth story, the lead player in sort of a new generation of athletic footwear and apparel companies.
zh: ON 是一个了不起的增长故事,是某种意义上的新一代运动鞋服公司的领跑者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that how you see ON as like the next?
zh: 你是这样看 ON 的吗,像是下一个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Big global brand.
zh: 大型全球品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you started with a unique sole design, which is also the way that Nike started with their waffle shoes.
zh: 我是说,你们是从一个独特的鞋底设计起步的,这也正是 Nike 当年靠他们的华夫饼鞋起步的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your plan?
zh: 你的计划是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the plan is to be the most premium global sports brand, really based on innovation.
zh: 我认为这个计划就是成为最高端(最 premium)的全球运动品牌,真正基于创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also on design.
zh: 但也基于设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end, it's about making sure that people are excited about sports, that they love to go out.
zh: 归根结底,是要确保人们对运动感到兴奋,让他们热爱走出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was out running at the Hudson this morning and it was so inspiring because there's such a big group of runners out there.
zh: 我今天早上在 Hudson 沿线跑步,那非常鼓舞人心,因为有那么一大群跑者在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think when you move, whether that's running or something else, something happens to your mind as well.
zh: 所以我认为当你运动时,无论是跑步还是别的什么,你的头脑也会发生一些变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really important for us via our mantra is dream on.
zh: 这对我们来说非常重要,我们的口号是「dream on」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that encapsulates it.
zh: 这句话概括了这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes I feel like when I go running here in New York, it's a race, even if there's not a race on, because there's so many people out running, right?
zh: 有时候我觉得我在纽约跑步时,就像在比赛一样,即使并没有比赛在进行,因为外面跑步的人太多了,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's New York pace, right?
zh: 这是纽约节奏,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to overtake each other.
zh: 你得互相超越。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the legacy players in this space, they sort of didn't seem to see the competition rising that you're part of.
zh: 我是说,这个领域里的老牌玩家,他们似乎没有看到你所处的这场竞争在崛起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Nike's struggling, Adidas seems to be finding its way a little bit.
zh: 我是说,Nike 正在挣扎,Adidas 似乎稍微找到了方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they're sort of the strivers, like...
zh: 你知道,他们算是那些奋斗者,比如……

speaker: Unknown
en: New Balance and Asics.
zh: New Balance 和 Asics。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there are other newer players like you, like Hoka, even apparel brands like Tracksmith or Bandit.
zh: 然后还有其他像你们这样的新玩家,比如 Hoka,甚至像 Tracksmith 或 Bandit 这样的服饰品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at that sort of competitive landscape, is there a specific spot that on hold?
zh: 当你审视这样的竞争格局时,ON 是否占据一个特定的位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that, where you fit in that ecosystem?
zh: 你怎么看待这件事,你们如何融入那个生态?

speaker: Unknown
en: When we started in 2010, we saw an opportunity to really innovate with a radical new idea, which was cloud tech.
zh: 当我们在 2010 年创立时,我们看到机会去用一个激进的新想法真正创新,那就是 cloud tech。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not just having an
zh: 它不仅仅是脚下垫一个……

speaker: Unknown
en: And foam a mattress underneath your foot, but engineering, really engineering the run and changing the feel of running.
zh: 泡棉床垫,而是工程化,真正工程化跑步,改变跑步的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we came always from an innovation space and I think that's the unique approach that we keep to this day.
zh: 所以我们一直是从创新的角度出发的,我认为这也是我们坚持至今的独特方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it also coincides with a radical shift that
zh: 而且我认为这也与一个激进的转变相吻合,

speaker: Unknown
en: Sports used to be, probably when we started, still something that you do on the weekend.
zh: 在我们创立之初,运动可能还是你在周末才做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now sports and sports lifestyle has moved to the center of society.
zh: 现在运动和运动生活方式已经移到了社会的中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think back in the days you had what I would call the leisure class.
zh: 我想在过去,有我会称之为「休闲阶层」(leisure class)的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very much about consumption.
zh: 那很大程度上是关于消费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about owning things.
zh: 是关于拥有物品。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that has changed, hasn't it, over the last 15 years?
zh: 但在过去 15 年里,这已经变了,不是吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a new movement class coming along.
zh: 我认为一个新的「运动阶层」(movement class)正在出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sports has moved to the very center of society.
zh: 运动已经移到了社会的最中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the last life moment.
zh: 它是最后一个生命时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what brings people together.
zh: 它是把人们凝聚在一起的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a lot more about experience.
zh: 而且它更多关乎体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about
zh: 它关乎

speaker: Unknown
en: Vitality.
zh: 活力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about longevity.
zh: 它关乎长寿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Health is the new wealth.
zh: 健康是新的财富。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think whenever society changed, it has created a big opportunity for absolutely new brands that respond to that to become big.
zh: 我认为每当社会发生变化，它都为那些响应这种变化的全新品牌创造了巨大的机会，让它们成长为大型品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the field that you're in, there are so many players.
zh: 在你所处的领域，有非常多的玩家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get inspired by each other.
zh: 他们互相启发。

speaker: Unknown
en: They steal each other's ideas.
zh: 他们互相窃取创意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it drive you crazy that you have to keep, oh, now someone else is trying to track what we were doing?
zh: 当你必须一直面对——哦，现在又有人在试图追踪我们在做的事情——这会不会让你抓狂？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I think that's exciting because then you always have to push yourself.
zh: 不，我觉得这很令人兴奋，因为这样你就必须一直鞭策自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: to create the next.
zh: 去创造下一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about the whole luxury space, the luxury space and the whole scarcity model, high price model, has over the last two years probably lost tens of millions of consumers who are looking for something that's more accessible.
zh: 如果你想想整个奢侈品领域，奢侈品领域和整个稀缺模式、高价模式，在过去两年里可能失去了数千万消费者，这些消费者在寻找更触手可及的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a huge opportunity for premium products as well.
zh: 而这对高端产品来说也是一个巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a premium product, but not necessarily a luxury product.
zh: 所以它是一个高端产品，但不一定是奢侈品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, because luxury is defined by limiting access.
zh: 是的，因为奢侈品的定义就是限制获取渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So scarcity, making it very exclusive.
zh: 也就是稀缺性，让它非常专属。

speaker: Unknown
en: On is defined by innovation.
zh: 而 On 的定义是创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to bring innovation to everyone to give you a better experience.
zh: 所以我们想把创新带给每一个人，给你更好的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, there's a certain price tag for innovation because we invest so much in creating the next.
zh: 当然，创新有一定的价格标签，因为我们在创造下一代产品上投入了非常多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that needs a premium brand that can invest
zh: 所以这需要一个能够投资的高端品牌

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're not a luxury brand at that end, but you're more a premium brand than some of the legacy players.
zh: 所以你在那一端不是奢侈品牌，但你比一些老牌玩家更偏高端品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, if you think about other areas of business, there was a moment very much defined by Newark.
zh: 我是说，如果你想想商业的其他领域，曾有一个由 Newark(纽瓦克)所定义的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: In New York, actually, when we learned that we can live in lofts and that kitchens move to the very center of our homes.
zh: 实际上是在纽约，当我们得知我们可以住在阁楼里，厨房搬到家的最中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: So home appliances became much more important.
zh: 于是家用电器变得重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you didn't kind of store your vacuum cleaner anymore in the closet back, but you hang it on your wall.
zh: 而你不再把吸尘器收到后面的壁橱里，而是把它挂在墙上。

speaker: Unknown
en: That created an opportunity for a brand to create something that is at the intersection of innovation, a chat engine in your vacuum cleaner, but also a unique aesthetic.
zh: 这就为一个品牌创造了机会，去创造处于创新交汇点的东西——你吸尘器里的一台聊天引擎(chát engine),以及一种独特的美学。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's a great example of a brand that is based on innovation but reaches millions of consumers.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个很好的例子：一个基于创新但触达数百万消费者的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have these relationships with celebrities.
zh: 你和名人有这些关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're plugged in with Zendaya, who's among this year's hottest stars.
zh: 你与 Zendaya 有深度绑定，她是今年最炙手可热的明星之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Roger Federer is a co-entrepreneur at the company.
zh: Roger Federer 是公司的共同创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did those relationships start?
zh: 这些关系是如何开始的？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot has been serendipity.
zh: 很多都是机缘巧合。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when Roger
zh: 所以当 Roger

speaker: Unknown
en: posted from Roland Garros on his Insta in an on shoe.
zh: 在他的 Insta 上从 Roland Garros 发布了一张穿着 On 鞋的照片。

speaker: Unknown
en: We felt that's an invitation to a date.
zh: 我们觉得那是一个约会的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we went on that date and that's how the relationship formed.
zh: 于是我们就赴了那次约会，这段关系就是这样形成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a little bit later, you probably remember that Zendaya had her Challengers movie.
zh: 然后稍晚一点，你可能还记得 Zendaya 有她的《Challengers》电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was, of course, about tennis.
zh: 而那当然是关于网球的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the characters was pretty much formed after Roger with his on-shoes.
zh: 其中一个角色基本上就是以 Roger 为原型塑造的，穿着他的 On 鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she always had to tie up these on-shoes because we had a special closing mechanism.
zh: 而她总是要系这些 On 鞋，因为我们有一个特殊的闭合机制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she, for her acting partner, was always lacing the shoes.
zh: 而她，为了她的演戏搭档，总是在给鞋子系带。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's how she got to know on, up close, and personal.
zh: 所以她就是这样近距离、亲身地认识了 On。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that started to form this relationship.
zh: 于是这就开始形成了这段关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's been very organic.
zh: 所以这一直都是非常自然有机的。

speaker: Unknown
en: With Roger, I understand you went to him and sort of pitched him even though you didn't have money for him.
zh: 关于 Roger,我了解到是你去找的他，向他做推介，尽管你当时没有钱请他。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I mean, we felt he first pitched us by putting on on his feet.
zh: 你知道，我是说，我们觉得是他先向我们做了推介——把 On 穿在了脚上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's Swiss, as you are.
zh: 而他是瑞士人，和你一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he's Swiss, and Switzerland is a small place.
zh: 他是瑞士人，而瑞士是个很小的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had some common friends.
zh: 所以我们有一些共同的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we went to a restaurant in the inner city of Zurich.
zh: 于是我们去了苏黎世市中心的一家餐厅。

speaker: Unknown
en: He came in with his baseball cap deep in his face and we hit it off and we had a great evening.
zh: 他戴着压得很低的棒球帽走进来，我们一见如故，度过了一个很棒的夜晚。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he was challenging us.
zh: 而他在挑战我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, hey, you've been such an amazing innovation player in running, really radically changing the feel of running.
zh: 他说，嘿，你们在跑步领域一直是非常了不起的创新者，真正彻底改变了跑步的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you change the feel of tennis as well and bring innovation to a tennis shoe as well?
zh: 你们能不能也改变网球的体验，把创新带进网球鞋里？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we did.
zh: 而这就是我们做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And three months later, we had him at our innovation space, which we call the Yon Labs in Zurich.
zh: 三个月后，我们把他请到了我们的创新空间，我们称之为苏黎世的 Yon Labs。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, and it was a good move on his part, too, because instead of taking money, I understand he took equity, and that has worked out very well for him, given how the company has grown.
zh: 嗯，对他来说这也是一步好棋，因为我了解到他没有拿钱，而是拿了股权，鉴于公司后来的成长，这对他来说非常划算。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it worked well.
zh: 我觉得这很成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were a seven-year-old company back then.
zh: 那时我们还是一家成立七年的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We felt
zh: 我们觉得

speaker: Unknown
en: Doing the classical model of just giving money to athletes, a classical endorsement model, that's not our way to do it.
zh: 走那种只给运动员钱的传统路子，即传统的代言模式，那不是我们的做事方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We always try to innovate on everything, not just on outsource, but also how you do the marketing model.
zh: 我们总是尝试在所有事情上创新，不只是外包创新，也包括你如何做营销模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we said, hey, instead of us giving you money, why don't you give us money?
zh: 所以我们说，嘿，与其我们给你钱，不如你给我们钱？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that worked out for everyone very well.
zh: 而这对每个人都非常划算。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your personal background is not shoe design.
zh: 你的个人背景并不是鞋类设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something you sort of came to, well, I don't know whether it was serendipity for you too.
zh: 这是某种你后来才涉足的领域，嗯，我不知道对你来说算不算也是一次机缘巧合。

speaker: Unknown
en: My background has always been in business, but especially in business when it comes to creativity, design, also digital.
zh: 我的背景一直是在商业领域，尤其是在涉及创意、设计以及数字化的商业领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a certain serendipity because a friend of Casper and me, my co-founder, his friend Olivier was a professional triathlete.
zh: 这确实是某种机缘巧合，因为 Casper 和我的一个朋友——我的联合创始人，他的朋友 Olivier 是一名职业铁人三项运动员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at some point Casper called me and said, hey, remember Olivier?
zh: 有一次 Casper 打电话给我说，嘿，还记得 Olivier 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: He had an idea for a shoe.
zh: 他有一个关于鞋子的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we said, ah.
zh: 我们说，啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Come on, that's crazy.
zh: 拜托，那太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we said, hey, let's try that shoe.
zh: 但后来我们说，嘿，让我们试试那双鞋吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was on a rainy day in Zurich, somewhere up in the woods.
zh: 那是在苏黎世一个下雨天，在树林里的某个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he came with the shoe that he had cut his garden hose at the home and glued these garden hose pieces underneath a shaved off shoe just to prove the principle.
zh: 他带来了那双鞋——他在家里把浇花用的水管剪断，把这些水管片段粘在一双削平的鞋底下，就为了证明这个原理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we went on a run and it felt amazing.
zh: 我们去跑了一次，感觉太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We felt, wow, that's really a different experience.
zh: 我们觉得，哇，这真是一种完全不同的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spent a fair amount of time with the former CEO of Nike, Mark Parker, who started as a shoe designer.
zh: 我和耐克前 CEO Mark Parker 相处过不少时间，他是从鞋类设计师做起的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, you didn't start as a shoe designer.
zh: 显然，你不是从鞋类设计师起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's more brand design really that you've been focused on.
zh: 你知道的，你真正专注的更多是品牌设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there something different about being a business leader when you're a designer?
zh: 当你是一名设计师时，作为商业领导者会有什么不同吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you look at the business in a different way?
zh: 你会以不同的方式看待这门生意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of the biggest brands have been created at that intersection of innovation and design.
zh: 一些最大的品牌正是在创新与设计的交汇处诞生的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about big leaps in the past, so for example, people started to travel at the end of the 19th century.
zh: 如果你回顾过去的一些重大跨越，比如，人们在 19 世纪末开始旅行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was a huge societal shift.
zh: 那是一次巨大的社会转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then some brands who had done probably some saddles for horses
zh: 然后一些可能以前做马鞍的牌子

speaker: Unknown
en: decided, hey, could we take our technology ladder, sometimes not even ladder, and create luggage that is very, very sturdy, that doesn't allow for moisture of coming in?
zh: 决定，嘿，我们能不能利用我们的技术积累，有时甚至算不上积累，去打造非常非常坚固、不让潮气进入的行李箱？

speaker: Unknown
en: And could we bring that to a new class?
zh: 我们能不能把它带给一个新阶层？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would call it the travel class.
zh: 我会称之为旅行阶层。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that created some of the biggest brands that today exist as the leading luxury brands.
zh: 而这造就了一些当今存在的一些最大的品牌，成为领先的奢侈品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: And similar things happened later on.
zh: 类似的事情后来也发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, when digital devices grew up from being either in the basement or then under your table and became portable and they became part of your identity because they're portable and you're sitting in the coffee shop with them or you're holding them to your ear.
zh: 比如，当数字设备从地下室或桌子底下长大，变得便携，并成为你身份的一部分——因为它们是便携的，你带着它们坐在咖啡店里，或者把它们举到耳边。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then design became much more important.
zh: 设计就变得重要得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's always that feel also for the consumer between the actual feeling, the sensation, but then also the emotional feeling, how this looks like, what does it say about me?
zh: 所以对消费者来说，始终存在那种感觉——既包括实际的触感、感官体验，也包括情感上的感受：它看起来怎么样，它说明了我是谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do I get excited to lace the shoes up and go for a run at the Hudson?
zh: 我会不会很兴奋地系好鞋带，去哈德逊河边跑个步？

speaker: Unknown
en: It should be a great feel, but it should also be a great emotional feel.
zh: 它应该有很好的体感，也应该有很好的情感体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that created some of the biggest brands.
zh: 所以我认为这造就了一些最大的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: David's reminder of brands that redefine themselves in the face of change.
zh: David 提醒我们那些在变革面前重新定义自己的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's instructive in our AI world that new capability and emotional impact should ideally reinforce each other.
zh: 在我们的 AI 世界里，新能力和情感影响力理想上应该相互强化，这一点很有启发意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what role do Ahn's physical stores play for David's brand?
zh: 那么 On 的实体店对 David 的品牌扮演了什么角色？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what prompted him to shake up the company's leadership earlier this year and take over as co-CEO?
zh: 又是什么促使他在今年早些时候调整公司领导层并接任联合 CEO?

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk about that and more after the break.
zh: 这些话题以及更多内容，我们将在广告之后继续讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stay with us.
zh: 请继续收听。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you've built substantial wealth through your business, it's often tied up in a single equity position.
zh: 当你通过自己的生意积累了可观的财富时，这些财富往往集中在单一的股权头寸上。

speaker: Unknown
en: The upside is real, but so is the risk, and knowing when to act isn't always obvious.
zh: 上行空间是真实的，但风险也是真实的，而知道何时行动并不总是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative planning works with business owners to build a strategy around concentrated equity, when to diversify, how to manage tax risk, and how to protect what you've spent years building.
zh: Creative planning 与企业主合作，围绕集中股权制定策略：何时多元化、如何管理税务风险、以及如何保护你多年积累的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Creative planning, where wealth works together.
zh: Creative planning,让财富协同运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at creativeplanning.com slash masters of scale.
zh: 了解更多请访问 creativeplanning.com slash masters of scale。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we get to the rest of our conversation today, I want to spend a moment sharing with you about Masters of Scale Summit, which returns to San Francisco this October 20th to 22nd.
zh: 在我们继续今天的对话之前，我想花一点时间向你介绍 Masters of Scale Summit,它将于今年 10 月 20 日至 22 日重返旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many of us feel overwhelmed right now.
zh: 我们中很多人都感到不堪重负。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like so much of the world is careening and we don't have power.
zh: 感觉世界上太多事情在失控，而我们没有权力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have agency.
zh: 我们没有主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the thing about the Masters of Scale Summit.
zh: 这正是 Masters of Scale Summit 的意义所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really designed to remind us that we do have agency, agency to lead, agency to design, to build the relationships and the partnerships that empower us and to make the change that we want to see.
zh: 它的真正设计初衷就是提醒我们：我们确实拥有主观能动性——去领导的主观能动性、去设计的主观能动性、去建立赋能我们的关系与伙伴关系、去实现我们想看到的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: We program a stage, we curate an audience, we set a schedule that builds in time for these relationships to be made and to grow so that by the time you leave Summit, you are fired out of a cannon, ready to run through walls to do better in the world.
zh: 我们策划舞台，我们精选听众，我们设置日程、为这些关系的建立和成长留出时间，这样当你离开 Summit 时，你就像从大炮里发射出去一样，准备好撞穿一堵堵墙，去把世界变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: With the agency that you actually have, I hope to see you there.
zh: 用你真正拥有的那种主观能动性。我希望在那里见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit mastersofscale.com slash summit.
zh: 访问 mastersofscale.com slash summit。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans will never be more intelligent than AI.
zh: 人类永远不会比 AI 更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's gonna be two types of companies.
zh: 将会有两种类型的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are great at AI and those that went out of business because they weren't.
zh: 一类是擅长 AI 的，另一类是因为不擅长而倒闭的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we build a future that is human-centered?
zh: 我们如何构建一个以人为本的未来？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Rana Elkayubi, and on my podcast, Pioneers of AI, we answer that question and so many more.
zh: 我是 Rana Elkayubi,在我的播客 Pioneers of AI 上，我们回答这个问题以及更多其他问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an AI scientist, entrepreneur, and investor, I know what it takes to build AI that works for everyone.
zh: 作为一名 AI 科学家、创业者和投资人，我知道构建对每个人都有效的 AI 需要什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every week, I sit down with the pioneers shaping our future, and we take you behind the scenes of the AI that's transforming our lives.
zh: 每周，我会与塑造我们未来的先锋们坐下来，带你深入了解那些正在改变我们生活的 AI 背后的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Find Pioneers of AI wherever you tune in.
zh: 在你收听播客的任何地方都可以找到 Pioneers of AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before the break, Anz David Alleman talked about the growing opportunity for new sports brands in today's marketplace.
zh: 在广告之前，On 的 David Alleman 谈到了当今市场上新运动品牌日益增长的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now he addresses the company's recent leadership shakeup, the role of brick and mortar stores in the digital world, and a crazy new shoe inspired by a YouTube Halloween video.
zh: 现在，他将谈到公司近期的领导层变动、实体店在数字世界中的角色，以及一款受 YouTube 万圣节视频启发的疯狂新鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus, does sustainability in footwear and apparel really matter?
zh: 另外，鞋类和服装的可持续性真的重要吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's hop back in.
zh: 让我们回到对话中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everything about Ahn's rise has always gone exactly the way you would want it to.
zh: On 的崛起并非一切都完全按你希望的方式进行。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, since going public five years ago, revenue has steadily gone up, you know, past $3 billion in 2025.
zh: 我的意思是，自从五年前上市以来，收入持续上升，你知道，在 2025 年突破了 30 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the stock price is down quite a bit from its peak.
zh: 但股价较峰值下跌了不少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And back in May, you and your co-founder, Casper, stepped into the co-CEO role, sort of shaking up Ahn's leadership.
zh: 而且在 5 月份，你和你的联合创始人 Casper 走上了联合 CEO 的岗位，算是重整了 On 的领导层。

speaker: Unknown
en: What prompted you to want to take a more hands-on control?
zh: 是什么促使你想要进行更直接的掌控？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at Anth's leadership model, we've always operated on very much as a partnership.
zh: 看 On 的领导模式，我们一直是以非常类似于伙伴关系的方式运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was several partners from the get-go.
zh: 所以从最初开始就是好几个合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Olivier Casper and I started the company as a partnership of three.
zh: 我的意思是,Olivier、Casper 和我以三人合伙的形式创立了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Later on, we were joined by other leaders.
zh: 后来，我们加入了其他领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, we were a partnership of five.
zh: 曾有一段时间，我们是五人合伙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was our secret weapon because it gave us an incredible bandwidth to go after very different missions.
zh: 而那是我们的秘密武器，因为它给了我们惊人的带宽去追求非常不同的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: So some of our partners went very much about operating the engine of the business, the supply chain, making sure that the machine is humming.
zh: 所以我们的一些合伙人主要负责运营业务的引擎，即供应链，确保机器平稳运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it gave us the opportunity to always stay focused on building the next
zh: 而这给了我们机会始终专注于打造下一个

speaker: Unknown
en: Growth engine.
zh: 增长引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So building the next shoe, building apparel, building retail, building a new sport like with Roger in tennis.
zh: 所以，打造下一款鞋、打造服装、打造零售、打造一项新运动，比如和 Roger 一起做网球。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very much what a founder-led organization should do, building the next.
zh: 这正是创始人主导的组织应该做的事：打造下一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in that transition that we had recently, that didn't change.
zh: 所以在我们最近的那次变动中，这一点没有改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: It shifted a little bit priorities.
zh: 只是优先级稍微转移了一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Operating the business and being very precise in the business has become a bigger share of our daily routine.
zh: 运营业务、在业务上做到非常精确，在我们日常工作中占了更大的比重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it frustrate you that with all the success you're having, like the stock prices, has not necessarily reflected that or the trajectory of that?
zh: 有了这么多的成功，比如股价却未必反映出这一点或这种发展轨迹，这会让你感到沮丧吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's just been a reality that there's been quite a bit of volatility in the market.
zh: 我认为这只是现实，市场上的波动确实相当大。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our way to navigate that is definitely not to resort to discounting, but to make sure that we bring the newest innovation into the sport.
zh: 而我们应对的方式绝对不是诉诸打折，而是确保我们把最新的创新带入这项运动。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned the word innovation several times, and I know that as businesses get bigger, it can often be harder to implement that innovation, that risk is harder for folks to take.
zh: 你几次提到“创新”这个词，我知道随着企业变大，实施创新往往会变得更难，人们承担风险的难度也更大。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wondered whether that was part of the motivation of sort of, you know, as a founder,
zh: 我想知道，这是不是你作为创始人的一部分动机，

speaker: Unknown
en: Being in that co-CE role to keep that moving along.
zh: 处于那种联席 CEO 的角色，来保持这种创新的持续推进。

speaker: Unknown
en: It definitely helps.
zh: 这肯定有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's always been our role as founders to make sure that we're not just thinking about the moment, but that we are thinking about the next moment.
zh: 作为创始人，我们的职责一直是确保我们不仅仅考虑当下，而是考虑下一个时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often people are coming to me and saying, hey, that's...
zh: 人们经常来找我，说，嘿，那真是……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible how you just exploded.
zh: 你们的爆发式增长真是令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm saying, yes, we've been a 16-year overnight success.
zh: 而我说，是的，我们是一场 16 年的一夜成名。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's true not just for the overall business, but it's often true then for the next thing that you add that's been often four or five years in the making.
zh: 这不仅适用于整个业务，往往也适用于你接下来增加的东西，那往往是酝酿了四五年的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, for example, our retail business, our stores, is now growing very fast, but actually came here to New York.
zh: 比如说，我们的零售业务、我们的门店，现在增长非常快，但实际上是来到纽约，

speaker: Unknown
en: to open the first store at Lafayette Street during COVID in 2021.
zh: 在 2021 年疫情期间在 Lafayette 街开设了第一家门店。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's five years ago.
zh: 所以那已经是五年前了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you're seeing really expanding and the business growing up with more than 80 stores open.
zh: 而现在你看到它真正在扩张，业务在成长，已经开设了超过 80 家门店。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember the folks at Warby Parker, when they first opened stores, it was much more of a branding priority for them than it was an actual sales priority.
zh: 我记得 Warby Parker 的人，当他们最初开设门店时，对他们来说这更像是一个品牌优先事项，而不是实际的销售优先事项。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they realized, actually, this is great business.
zh: 而他们意识到，其实，这是门好生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: For you guys, did it start that way?
zh: 对你们来说，一开始是这样吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Was it more like, oh, we're going to brand ourselves like some other brands have these stores?
zh: 是不是更像是，哦，我们要像其他品牌那样用门店来做品牌？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or did you always think like, oh, this is a financial lever too?
zh: 还是你一直认为，哦，这也是一个财务杠杆？

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, the primary reason to start stores has been two things.
zh: 对我们来说，开设门店的主要原因有两点。

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, we wanted to plant the brand in the middle of society and our city centers still are very much in the middle of society.
zh: 首先，我们想把品牌植根于社会的中心，而我们的市中心仍然是社会的中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It probably wasn't so obvious in the middle of the pandemic.
zh: 在疫情最严重的时候，这可能不太明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you got better rents then, I guess.
zh: 但那时候租金应该更好，我猜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, absolutely true.
zh: 是的，绝对正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we continue to believe that after COVID, city centers are coming back.
zh: 而且我们一直相信，疫情之后，市中心会回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we invested very much then in, hey, this is our opportunity to go in.
zh: 所以我们当时大力投资，心想，嘿，这是我们进军的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second reason has been we were very clear that we want to become a brand that is, as we call it, toe to head.
zh: 第二个原因是我们非常清楚，我们想成为一个像我们所说的“从头到脚”的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started to invest into apparel.
zh: 于是我们开始投资服装。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's very hard to just do apparel in a shoe wall in one of our partner stores.
zh: 而只在我们合作门店的一面鞋墙里做服装是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you have to give it the full expression.
zh: 所以我认为你必须给它完整的呈现。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you can control the environment much more.
zh: 因为你可以更多地控制环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, we can control the expression and especially for something like apparel where you can't just put the shoe on a wall as a freestanding object, but where you have to give it space.
zh: 是的，我们可以控制呈现方式，尤其是像服装这样的东西，你不能只是把鞋作为一个独立的物体放在墙上，而是必须给它空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a huge opportunity for retail as well.
zh: 这对零售来说也是一个巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And does that then drive the retail sales of the apparel even not in your stores?
zh: 那么这是否会推动服装的零售销售，即使不是在你的门店里？

speaker: Unknown
en: It does.
zh: 确实如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, I mean, retail stores lift all boats.
zh: 我是说，零售门店能水涨船高。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it just gives additional energy to a community in the city.
zh: 它给城市里的一个社区带来了额外的活力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also do a lot of runs out of the store.
zh: 我们也会从门店组织很多跑步活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that journey, we found out it's a great business as well.
zh: 在这个过程中，我们发现它也是一门很好的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that was not the first thought.
zh: 但那并不是最初的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the outcome of doing all the right things, how you go into retail.
zh: 它是正确地做所有进入零售的事情的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is this race in athletic footwear to use more technology.
zh: 在运动鞋领域存在一场使用更多技术的竞赛。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Brooks created a special shoe to help Josh Kerr break the record for the mile run.
zh: 我是说，Brooks 打造了一款特制的鞋，帮助 Josh Kerr 打破了一英里跑的纪录。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about tech at on?
zh: 你如何看待 On 的技术？

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw a video of this light spray machine that you're using for a particular shoe, which is pretty cool.
zh: 我看过一个视频，是你们用于某款鞋的喷雾机器，相当酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I have a...
zh: 我想我有一个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's the shoe.
zh: 这是那双鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often there are 200 pieces going into an upper of a shoe.
zh: 通常一只鞋的鞋面有200个部件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a very classical manufacturing method with 200 steps until you have a full shoe together.
zh: 所以这是一种非常经典的制造方法，要经过200道工序才能把一只完整的鞋组装起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had a young designer who had seen a YouTube video of somebody with a hot glue gun spraying a Halloween net.
zh: 当时我们有一位年轻的设计师，他看过一个 YouTube 视频，视频里有人用热熔胶枪喷涂一个万圣节网罩。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was his inspiration.
zh: 那就是他的灵感来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, hey, if somebody can spray a Halloween net, could I use a hot glue gun to spray a shoe as well?
zh: 他说，嘿，如果有人能喷涂一个万圣节网罩，那我是不是也能用热熔胶枪来喷一只鞋？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he did that.
zh: 他就这么做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had a very scrappy first prototype of that.
zh: 我们做出了一个非常粗糙的第一个原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he reminded us of that shoe where Olivier had put the garden hose pieces.
zh: 他还提醒我们想起那双 Olivier 放上花园水管部件的鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And back then, we took a conscious decision to embrace a lot of risk and say, hey, it sounds crazy.
zh: 当年，我们有意识地做了一个拥抱大量风险的决定，说：嘿，这听起来很疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But crazy is good because the night is always the darkest before dawn.
zh: 鞋面因为不是经过200道工序，而是一道工序，

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we said, hey, let's put a few robotics engineers, material scientists, sports scientists around that designer.
zh: 于是我们说，嘿，让我们在那位设计师周围配置几名机器人工程师、材料科学家和运动科学家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we had a small attack team of five people that then came up with light spray, which is a technology…
zh: 于是我们有了一支五人的小型突击队，他们随后开发出了 light spray 这项技术……

speaker: Unknown
en: where you have a robotic arm and that robotic arm sprays a small filament in polygonic shapes directly on an outsole so it's not stitched on it just melts with the outsole and it collapses this process of 200 steps into one.
zh: 用一个机械臂，把一小股丝线以多边形形状直接喷涂在外底上，所以它不是缝上去的，而是直接与外底熔合在一起，它把这道200步的工序压缩成了一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a shoe that is sprayed by a robotic arm in three minutes.
zh: 这是一双由机械臂在三分钟内喷涂出来的鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: When an idea like this comes to you, I mean, you must get lots of proposals for crazy, new, like, how do you decide what you're gonna invest in?
zh: 当这样的想法出现在你面前时，我是说，你们肯定会收到很多疯狂的、新颖的提案，你们是怎么决定要投资哪一项的？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a whole pipeline process.
zh: 我们有一整套流水线流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So probably have, at any given point,
zh: 所以在任何时点，我们大概都有

speaker: Unknown
en: 50, 100 ideas what we could do.
zh: 50到100个可以去做想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we have review meetings where we're basically saying, hey, what is good to go and stage gates and decide what goes down the innovation funnel.
zh: 然后我们有评审会议，基本上是在说，嘿，哪些可以进入下一阶段，设置阶段门，决定哪些进入创新漏斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's our standard procedure.
zh: 这是我们的标准流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: You connected with this sort of focused customer base of runners.
zh: 你们与跑者这样一个聚焦的客户群体建立了联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you try to expand, you have to reach a broader community beyond that sort of more elite community.
zh: 而当你们试图扩张时，你们必须触及比那个更精英的群体更广泛的社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you test how far you can go with the brand and what the base is willing to let you do that allows you to still maintain your credibility with them because you don't want them to move off to the next new hot shoe brand?
zh: 你们如何测试这个品牌能走多远、这个基础群体愿意让你们做什么，同时又让你们能继续维持对他们的可信度？因为你们不希望他们流向下一个热门的新鞋品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, that's absolutely true.
zh: 不，这完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the athlete for us comes always first.
zh: 对我们来说，运动员永远排在第一位。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are operating with the On Athletic Club, one of the largest athlete group in the industry with runners, sprinters.
zh: 我们与 On Athletic Club 合作，它是行业内规模最大的运动员团体之一，拥有长跑运动员、短跑运动员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a dedicated team.
zh: 所以我们有一个专门的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's our core.
zh: 那是我们的核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the same token, our lens is not running, but it's movement.
zh: 同样地，我们的视角不是跑步，而是运动(movement)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we feel movement is more important than ever because it's not just about health and longevity and vitality, topics that are incredibly important, but it's also about what happens to your mind.
zh: 所以我们觉得运动比以往任何时候都更重要，因为这不仅关乎健康、长寿和活力这些极其重要的话题，还关乎你的心智会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We feel when you're going out, whether that's now running or
zh: 我们觉得当你出门时，无论是现在去跑步，还是

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's training or whether it's tennis or whether it's any or hiking or any other form of movement, something happens to your mind.
zh: 无论是训练，无论是打网球，无论是远足还是任何其他形式的运动，你的心智都会发生一些变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You come back probably with either a new idea, a bit more optimistic, and we started in running, but of course we're expanding in all other sports of movement.
zh: 你回来时可能带着一个新想法，或者更乐观了一些。我们从跑步起步，但当然，我们正在扩展到其他所有的运动形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did want to ask you about sustainability in your brand.
zh: 我确实想问一下你们品牌的可持续发展问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Swiss have a very strong reputation for sustainability here in the U.S.
zh: 瑞士人在美国这里有着非常好的可持续发展声誉。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of become kind of a dormant conversation a little bit.
zh: 这在一定程度上已经变成一个有点沉寂的话题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you have your clean cloud shirts that are made from carbon emissions.
zh: 我知道你们有 Clean Cloud 衬衫，是用碳排放制成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure how that works.
zh: 我不太清楚那是怎么运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does being green matter today in the marketplace, in how you sell, or is it a separate consideration?
zh: 在今天的市场上、在你们的销售中，环保重要吗？还是说它是一个单独的考量？

speaker: Unknown
en: It matters very much to us.
zh: 它对我们非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Switzerland is a bit the pinnacle of an outdoor theme park.
zh: 我认为瑞士有点像户外主题公园的巅峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we do most of our sports in nature.
zh: 所以我们大部分的运动都是在自然中进行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that we have to preserve.
zh: 这是我们必须保护的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so on every dimension that we can do to reduce the footprint of on towards the environment is super important.
zh: 所以在每一个我们能做的维度上，减少 On 对环境的足迹都极其重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And take a light spray shoe.
zh: 拿一双 light spray 鞋来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: The shoe upper is because it's not 200 steps going into it, but one step.
zh: 鞋面是因为它不是 200 步进入其中,而是一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: is more than 75% lower CO2 footprint.
zh: 其碳足迹降低了75%以上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or you mentioned clean cloud.
zh: 或者你提到的 clean cloud。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're actually sucking bad clouds from the air industry emissions, create the base ingredients for foam again to create clean cloud foam.
zh: 我们实际上是在从航空业的排放中吸取坏云，再次制造出泡沫的基础原料，用来制作 clean cloud 泡沫。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do everything that innovation can do to lower the footprint.
zh: 所以我们竭尽创新所能来降低足迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you've been on this 16-year overnight success journey.
zh: 所以你走过了这段 16 年的一夜成名之旅。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's at stake for ON right now?
zh: 现在对 ON 来说，利害攸关的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The defining decade, Foran, is ahead of us.
zh: Foran，决定性的十年就在我们前方。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've planted so many seeds that are growing up, which is exciting.
zh: 我们种下了很多正在成长的种子，这令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our apparel, it's growing more than 50% year over year.
zh: 我们的服装业务，同比增长超过 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our digital channels.
zh: 我们的数字渠道。

speaker: Unknown
en: are growing very fast.
zh: 增长非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're expanding globally, so we're relevant for communities across the globe.
zh: 我们正在全球扩张，所以我们对全球各地的社区都有相关性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're still the fastest growing brand in our industry of the scaled sports brands.
zh: 在规模化的运动品牌中，我们仍然是我们行业里增长最快的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also the most premium in terms of margins, the most premium brand.
zh: 在利润率方面，我们也是最顶尖的，最高端的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really an opportunity to build a brand that doesn't have to be ultimately the absolute biggest, but is the most premium brand of the future.
zh: 所以这真的是一个机会，去打造一个不一定非要成为绝对最大的、但将成为未来最高端品牌的品牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, David, I have to say, this has been a great conversation.
zh: 好的，David，我必须说，这是一次很棒的对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks so much for joining me and doing it.
zh: 非常感谢你参与并完成这次节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you very much for having me.
zh: 非常感谢你邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep going back to that light spray shoe that David talked about.
zh: 我一直惦记着 David 谈到的那只轻喷 shoe。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was so light in my hand.
zh: 它在我手里非常轻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of crazy.
zh: 有点不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, maybe it won't revolutionize shoemaking.
zh: 现在，也许它不会彻底改变制鞋业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who knows?
zh: 谁知道呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: But David's emphasis on rethinking and creativity, that's the threat that any renegade business poses.
zh: 但 David 对重新思考和创造力的强调，正是任何叛逆企业构成的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's what even the biggest companies need to embrace, particularly right now.
zh: 而这也是即使最大的公司都需要拥抱的东西，尤其是现在。

speaker: Unknown
en: David isn't saying that he's going after the sports giants at Nike and Adidas, but of course, why would he?
zh: David 并没有说他要挑战 Nike 和 Adidas 这些运动巨头，但当然，他为什么要呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: That just complicates investor expectations.
zh: 那只会让投资者的预期变得更复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still, in his very Swiss way, you can hear his ambition.
zh: 尽管如此，以他非常瑞士的方式，你能听出他的雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: He may not be at the very front of the pack, but he can see the leaders ahead, and he knows the race is long.
zh: 他也许不在队伍的最前面，但他能看见前方的领跑者，而且他知道这场比赛很长。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm Bob Safian.
zh: 我是 Bob Safian。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for listening.
zh: 感谢收听。

en: Hey listeners, Bob here.
zh: 各位听众，我是 Bob。

zh: 希望在那里见到你。
